Then the merchant's son Sudhana — striving to purify the bodhisattva's victory and diligence; his mind made exceedingly bright by the light of the bodhisattva's powers; possessed of a heart that, like a steadfast bodhisattva, cannot be overcome by others and is resolute; his mind undaunted through the excellent armour of the bodhisattva's aspiration; striving to abide in and fully increase the bodhisattva's firm intention; possessed of the intention to hold the rain from the cloud of the bodhisattva's conduct; possessed of a mind-stream never sated by the rain from the bodhisattva's Dharma-cloud; manifest in the aspiration to enter all the bodhisattva's qualities; wishing to give himself up entirely to gather in all beings by guiding them; wishing to rescue all beings from the great wilderness of saṃsāra; never sated in seeing, hearing and attending upon spiritual friends; possessed of the generation of immeasurable service to the Dharma — bowed his head to the two feet of the monk Sudarśana, circumambulated the monk Sudarśana to the right many hundreds of thousands of times, looked at him again and again, and departed from the presence of the monk Sudarśana.
